entry.englishMeaning: the practical possibility of carrying out a plan
entry.coreIdea: Check whether the plan can realistically be carried out.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract noun for whether a plan can realistically be carried out under the circumstances.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: assessing feasibility can lead to either acceptance or rejection.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Cautious and practical here: the speaker wants to check whether the December timing is achievable.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Relatively formal and common in planning. “Whether we can realistically do it” is a simpler explanation.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: We need to assess the feasibility of finishing before December.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: the practical possibility of carrying out a plan
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The team needs to determine whether finishing before December is achievable under the actual constraints.

when_to_use: Assess whether time, resources, technology or other constraints allow a proposed plan to be carried out.
when_not_to_use: Do not use feasibility as a synonym for desirability: a possible plan may still be a poor choice.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: assess the feasibility of + noun / gerund; a feasibility study

examples.example_1: We need to assess the feasibility of finishing before December.
examples.example_2: The club investigated the feasibility of running evening classes with its current volunteers.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Everyone likes the idea of a weekend event.
B: We still need to check its feasibility. Do we have a venue and enough volunteers?
A: I will check both.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: We assessed the feasibility to finish by Friday.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use feasibility of finishing: We assessed the feasibility of finishing by Friday.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Feasibility concerns whether a plan can be done; desirability concerns whether it is worth choosing.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Check the calendar, budget and available people before committing.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: We must check the feasibility of opening on Sundays.
memory_practice.recall_question: Can a plan be feasible without being desirable?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Check whether resources allow the plan. B: Ask whether people like its appearance. Which directly assesses feasibility?
memory_practice.production_task: Name two constraints you would examine when assessing the feasibility of a weekend workshop.

advanced_nuance: Feasibility is relative to stated conditions. A plan may be feasible with more staff but not with the current team, so an assessment should name the assumptions behind its conclusion.

entry.englishMeaning: to twist or move uneasily because of discomfort or embarrassment
entry.coreIdea: Move uneasily because you feel uncomfortable or embarrassed.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Literal verb for uneasy twisting or movement, used here to suggest the discomfort or embarrassment someone might be made to feel.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Negative in this context because causing another person discomfort is presented as an unhelpful aim.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Self-questioning here: the speaker rejects making the other person squirm as the purpose of the interaction.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Expressive general vocabulary. “Make someone uncomfortable” is plainer when no physical movement is intended.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Oh  yeah,  I  guess  it's  not  to  make  the  other  person  squirm  or  to  preen  in  fr ont  of  a  crowd .
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to twist or move uneasily because of discomfort or embarrassment
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker rejects causing the other person embarrassment or discomfort as the aim of the interaction.

when_to_use: Describe uneasy twisting or movement caused by discomfort, or vividly describe someone's embarrassment.
when_not_to_use: For relaxed movement with no discomfort, use shift position rather than implying that the person squirms.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: squirm in + seat; squirm with + embarrassment; make someone squirm

examples.example_1: The unexpected question made him squirm in his chair.
examples.example_2: I squirm with embarrassment whenever that old recording is played.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Did you notice how uncomfortable he looked?
B: Yes. That personal question made him squirm.
A: We should return to the issue instead of embarrassing him.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: The question made him to squirm.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: The question made him squirm. After made plus object, use the base verb without to.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Squirm suggests uneasy movement or embarrassment; fidget can describe restless movements without implying embarrassment.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Someone twists in their chair when an embarrassing question is asked.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The awkward personal question made me squirm.
memory_practice.recall_question: What feeling often accompanies squirming in this conversational sense?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Twist uncomfortably under an embarrassing question. B: Sit back comfortably after a pleasant meal. Which fits squirm?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe a fictional question that makes a character squirm, then give a more considerate way to raise the issue.

advanced_nuance: Make someone squirm can describe emotional discomfort even when no literal twisting is observed. The source uses it to question an unhelpful conversational aim, not to recommend humiliation.

entry.englishMeaning: when reconsidering a past event from the present
entry.coreIdea: Look back using what you know now.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Discourse phrase for looking back at a past event with present knowledge.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: the later judgement may involve approval, regret or a changed view.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Reflective and approving here: the speaker now judges the smaller venue to have been the better option.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral to formal; common in reviews and reflective writing. “Looking back” sounds more conversational.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: In retrospect, the smaller venue was the better choice.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: when reconsidering a past event from the present
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker now judges the smaller venue to have been the better choice after reconsidering the past decision.

when_to_use: Reassess a past decision or event with knowledge gained afterward.
when_not_to_use: For a prediction about an event that has not happened, use looking ahead rather than in retrospect.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: In retrospect, + judgement about a past event

examples.example_1: In retrospect, the smaller venue was the better choice.
examples.example_2: The early warning signs seem obvious in retrospect, although we missed them at the time.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Would you choose the same route again?
B: In retrospect, the train would have been easier.
A: We did not know how bad the traffic would be.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Using in retrospect for a future prediction rather than a review of the past.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use in retrospect to look back: In retrospect, we should have booked earlier.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: In retrospect uses present knowledge to reassess the past; at the time describes the knowledge or view held then.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Turn back to an old decision with new information in your hand.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: In retrospect, asking for help earlier would have saved time.
memory_practice.recall_question: What knowledge might you have in retrospect that you lacked at the time?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Review last month's decision using its results. B: Predict next year's results before they occur. Which is retrospective?
memory_practice.production_task: Review an invented planning decision using in retrospect, and explain one fact that became clear only later.

advanced_nuance: In retrospect does not always express regret: it can confirm that a decision was good. It also reminds readers that present knowledge may make an earlier choice look easier than it actually was.

entry.englishMeaning: to keep a discussion focused on its intended subject
entry.coreIdea: Keep the discussion focused on the intended subject.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Conversational instruction to keep discussing the intended subject rather than move into unrelated matters.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral about focus, but it may imply that the discussion is beginning to wander.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Firm and practical here: the speaker directs attention back to resolving the staffing question first.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in meetings, teaching and everyday discussion. A softer request can name the topic to return to.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: We need to stay on topic and settle the staffing question first.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to keep a discussion focused on its intended subject
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker asks the group to focus on the staffing question and resolve it before turning to other matters.

when_to_use: Guide a conversation back to its agreed subject when unrelated issues are distracting the group.
when_not_to_use: Do not dismiss a relevant concern as off-topic simply because it challenges your view; explain how the discussion's scope is defined.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: stay on topic; help someone stay on topic; stay on topic and + intended action
common_collocations: help the group stay on topic

examples.example_1: We need to stay on topic and settle the staffing question first.
examples.example_2: The teacher used a short outline to help the class stay on topic during the debate.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: This reminds me of a completely different event.
B: Could we stay on topic and finish the staffing question first?
A: Yes, I will save that story for later.

mistakes_differences.correction: Say: Please stay on topic. On is the usual preposition in this expression.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Stay on topic concerns relevance; keep it brief concerns length. A long contribution can remain relevant, and a short one can still be off-topic.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Bring a wandering discussion back to the heading on the agenda.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Let us stay on topic until we have agreed the next step.
memory_practice.recall_question: Does stay on topic ask for relevance, brevity or both automatically?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Discuss the evidence relevant to the agreed question. B: Tell an unrelated short anecdote. Which stays on topic?
memory_practice.production_task: Write a polite request to stay on topic, naming the issue to finish and offering a later time for the new issue.

advanced_nuance: Stay on topic can sound corrective or dismissive if used abruptly. Naming the shared goal and acknowledging the other point helps make it a cooperative request.

entry.englishMeaning: a record of decisions and the reasons for making them
entry.coreIdea: Record what was decided and why.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Professional noun phrase for a record of decisions and their supporting reasons.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: keeping a log supports traceability without proving that the decisions themselves were sound.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Polite and procedural here: “Please add” requests a specific record update.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common project-management wording. “Record of decisions” is clearer outside that setting.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Please add the revised deadline to the decision log.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a record of decisions and the reasons for making them
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker asks for the changed deadline to be entered in the record of decisions.

when_to_use: Refer to a maintained record of decisions and their reasons so others can understand or revisit them later.
when_not_to_use: Do not call a list of unresolved questions a decision log unless it clearly distinguishes those questions from decisions already made.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: add something to / update / consult + the decision log
common_collocations: an entry in the decision log

examples.example_1: Please add the revised deadline to the decision log.
examples.example_2: The new coordinator checked the decision log to understand why the event had moved indoors.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Why did we choose the smaller room?
B: The reason is in the decision log: we needed step-free access.
A: That explains the choice.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Recording an undecided suggestion as though it were an agreed decision in the decision log.
mistakes_differences.correction: Record the agreed decision and its reason in the decision log; label unresolved proposals separately.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A decision log records choices and their reasons; a task list records work to do. One decision can create several tasks.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Beside each agreed choice, write why the group chose it.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The decision log explains why we changed the deadline.
memory_practice.recall_question: What should a decision log explain beyond the chosen option?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: The selected venue and the reason for choosing it. B: A list of possible venues with no selection. Which is ready for the decision log?
memory_practice.production_task: Write a short decision-log entry for a fictional schedule change, including the decision and its reason.

advanced_nuance: A decision log preserves reasoning for later readers, but it does not prove the choice remains right. If conditions change, record the new decision without silently erasing the earlier rationale.

entry.englishMeaning: a very sad or disastrous event
entry.coreIdea: A deeply sad event brings serious loss or suffering.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract noun for a deeply sad or disastrous event, emphasizing its human seriousness.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Strongly negative: it conveys grave loss or suffering rather than an ordinary inconvenience.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Shocked or distressed here: asking how it could happen suggests difficulty accepting or understanding the event.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in serious reporting and personal reactions. Using it for a minor setback can sound exaggerated or insensitive.

meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a very sad or disastrous event
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker reacts with distress or disbelief to a serious event. The short question does not identify what happened.

when_to_use: Describe an event involving grave loss or suffering, especially when emphasising its human impact.
when_not_to_use: Calling an ordinary inconvenience a tragedy can sound exaggerated or insensitive when serious suffering is being discussed.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: a tragedy for + people; the tragedy of + event; prevent / mourn + a tragedy

examples.example_1: The village came together to support the families after the tragedy.
examples.example_2: The novel explores how one family rebuilds its life after a personal tragedy.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: How are the families coping after the tragedy?
B: Their neighbours are helping with everyday needs.
A: We should ask what support would be useful.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Treating tragedy as a neutral word for any small problem.
mistakes_differences.correction: Reserve tragedy for serious loss or suffering unless an exaggerated, humorous use is clearly intended and appropriate.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A setback interrupts progress; a tragedy emphasises grave suffering or loss. The terms carry very different emotional weight.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A community gathers to support people after a devastating loss.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The tragedy affected the whole community.
memory_practice.recall_question: Why is tragedy stronger than inconvenience?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A minor delay with no serious harm. B: An event causing grave loss to a community. Which warrants tragedy in serious reporting?
memory_practice.production_task: Write a respectful fictional sentence about a community supporting people after a tragedy, without adding sensational details.

advanced_nuance: Tragedy conveys the speaker's sense of profound loss, but does not by itself establish cause or responsibility. A careful account separates that emotional description from factual explanations.

meaning_usage_profile.tone: Lightly descriptive here: “seated neatly atop” makes the anatomical position easy to picture.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Tw o  tiny  organs  seated  neatly  atop  your  kidneys  pump  adrenaline  into your  bloodstream.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: in a tidy, orderly, or precise way

entry.coreIdea: Emotion or enthusiasm seems excessive or sentimental.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract adjective for emotion or enthusiasm presented as excessive or sentimental.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Negative or dismissive: it makes the emotional quality sound less serious or credible.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Ironic and skeptical in the proposition voiced here: the passage contrasts “soft-and-gushy” conversation with the financial bottom line.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Informal and judgemental. “Emotionally expressive” is more neutral when excessive sentiment is not intended.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Surely  a  soft-and­ gushy  factor  such  as  how  you  talk  to  one  another  doesn't  have  an  impact  on  the  not  so  soft-and-gushy  bottom  line.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The wording dismissively presents interpersonal communication as soft and sentimental, contrasting it with financial results.

when_to_use: Informally criticise praise, sentiment or enthusiasm that seems excessive to the speaker.
when_not_to_use: For neutral description of warmth or enthusiasm, use affectionate or enthusiastic rather than adding the criticism implied by gushy.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: a gushy + message / tribute / review; sound / seem + gushy

examples.example_1: The review was so gushy that it barely mentioned any details about the performance.
examples.example_2: He wanted to write a warm thank-you note without sounding gushy.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Does this thank-you message sound sincere?
B: The repeated superlatives make it a little gushy.
A: I will mention one specific thing I appreciated instead.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Using gushy as an entirely neutral synonym for kind.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use gushy when you intend to suggest excessive sentiment or enthusiasm; kind does not carry that criticism.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Warm praise can be measured and specific; gushy praise suggests emotional enthusiasm that the speaker considers excessive.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A short message overflows with superlatives and sentimental declarations.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: I wanted the note to be warm rather than gushy.
memory_practice.recall_question: What judgement does gushy add to enthusiastic?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A restrained thank-you naming one helpful action. B: Repeated extravagant declarations of admiration. Which is more likely to be called gushy?
memory_practice.production_task: Rewrite an exaggerated thank-you note so it remains warm but less gushy, using one concrete detail.

advanced_nuance: Gushy is informal and subjective: a message one reader finds affectionate may seem excessive to another. The source uses that dismissive flavour in a contrast with supposedly harder financial concerns.

entry.englishMeaning: a change over time in data or in the relationship a model has learned
entry.coreIdea: Data or learned relationships change after a model is deployed.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Technical noun for changes over time in data or learned relationships that can affect a model.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Cautionary in this setting because drift may require monitoring or updates; change is not automatically evidence of failure.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Procedural and forward-looking here: the speaker lists maintenance activities after deployment.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Standard machine-learning terminology. Explain what is changing rather than rely on “drift” alone with a general audience.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Now that it's live, we need to monitor and maintain it, and this means we'll be tracking the performance, detecting drift, and updating the model if needed.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a change over time in data or in the relationship a model has learned
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker lists detecting changes over time as part of maintaining a live model, alongside tracking performance and making updates when needed.

when_to_use: Discuss changes in incoming data or relevant relationships over time in a deployed modelling system.
when_not_to_use: Do not call every isolated prediction error drift; a single error does not establish a change over time.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: detect / monitor / investigate + drift; drift in + data / input distribution

examples.example_1: The team monitors drift in incoming data after the model goes live.
examples.example_2: A change in how customers filled out the form prompted an investigation of possible drift.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Why are the new inputs different from the training sample?
B: There may be drift in how users complete the form.
A: Let us compare the patterns and check performance before changing the model.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Declaring drift solely because one prediction was wrong.
mistakes_differences.correction: Investigate changes across time and relevant data; one wrong prediction alone does not establish drift.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A prediction error concerns one output's correctness; drift concerns change over time in data or relevant relationships.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: The data arriving today gradually differs from the data used before.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: We monitor drift as part of maintaining the deployed model.
memory_practice.recall_question: Why is a single wrong prediction insufficient evidence of drift?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: The incoming-data pattern shifts over several months. B: One isolated prediction is wrong with no observed change. Which directly suggests drift?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe a fictional change in user behaviour that could lead a team to investigate drift in a deployed model.

advanced_nuance: Drift does not automatically imply that the model is unusable. Its importance depends on what changed and how that change affects the task, so detection and evaluation are separate steps.

entry.englishMeaning: a very funny or entertaining person, event, or experience
entry.coreIdea: Something or someone is very funny or entertaining.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Figurative informal expression for something very funny or entertaining.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive: it conveys that the experience provided considerable amusement.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Amused and approving here: the short statement directly evaluates the experience as entertaining.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Informal and sometimes playfully old-fashioned. “Very funny” or “great fun” is more widely neutral.

meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a very funny or entertaining person, event, or experience
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker evaluates the experience as highly amusing. The short statement does not identify the event.

when_to_use: Informally describe a funny person, event or experience with cheerful approval.
when_not_to_use: For a solemn event or a formal evaluation, choose wording that fits the seriousness and audience rather than the playful a hoot.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: be a hoot; someone / something was a hoot

examples.example_1: The improvised puppet show was a hoot.
examples.example_2: Your uncle is a hoot; his stories kept everyone laughing.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: How was the comedy workshop?
B: It was a hoot. We laughed through most of the exercises.
A: I might join you next time.

mistakes_differences.correction: Say: The show was a hoot. Include the article in this countable informal expression.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A hoot suggests strong amusement; interesting can describe something engaging without saying it is funny.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: An entertaining story has everyone laughing around the table.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The amateur comedy show was a hoot.
memory_practice.recall_question: Does a hoot praise something as amusing or merely informative?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A funny performance that keeps the audience laughing. B: A useful but solemn technical briefing. Which is more naturally a hoot?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe a fictional entertaining event using a hoot, and add one detail explaining why it was funny.

advanced_nuance: A hoot has a playful, informal flavour and can sound deliberately old-fashioned. In this use it evaluates amusement; it is not a literal description of a bird's call.
